summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived history of the Mexican state of Chihuahua. It covers its 1820s-1830s political upheavals, the Mexican-American War battles fought in the state (El Bracito, Sacramento, Santa Cruz de los Rosales) and the American occupation of the capital until May 22, 1848, the Hidalgo and independence-day commemorations, the 1910 start of the Revolution at Cuchillo Parado, and the state's population and climate.
one_line: A history and overview of the Mexican state of Chihuahua, covering the Mexican-American War battles, 19th-century politics, the 1910 Revolution start, population and desert climate.
key_facts: The United States Congress declared war on Mexico on May 13, 1846, after only a few hours of debate.
Mexico officially declared war by Congress on July 7, 1846, after President Jose Mariano Paredes issued a manifesto on May 23.
Chihuahua sent 12,000 men led by Colonel Vidal to the border to stop the American military advance into the state.
The battle of El Bracito on December 25, 1846 pitted 500 Mexican cavalry and 70 infantry against 1,100-1,200 Americans, and the Mexican forces were forced to retreat.
General Doniphan left El Paso del Norte on February 8, 1847 with 924 men, mostly from Missouri, accompanying a train of 315 wagons.
The Battle of Sacramento was the sole defense of the state capital; almost 300 Mexicans were killed, almost 300 were wounded, and 400 were taken prisoner.
The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, signed February 2, 1848 by Nicholas Trist, ended the war, gave the U.S. undisputed control of Texas, and established the Rio Grande as the U.S.-Mexican border.
The Battle of Santa Cruz de los Rosales, fought March 16, 1848 near Santa Cruz de los Rosales, was the last battle of the Mexican-American War and occurred after the peace treaty was signed.
American forces occupied the state capital until May 22, 1848.
The Chihuahua legislature was not installed until May 1, 1826, after disputed elections for the first regular legislature.
In February 1830, Gaspar de Ochoa aligned with Anastasio Bustamante and organized an opposition group that arrested the new governor, F. Elorriaga.
September 16, 1810 became the officially recognized day of Mexican independence, reflecting the favoring of the liberal Hidalgo over the conservative Iturbide.
Toribio Ortega, a Madero supporter, took up arms with a group of followers at Cuchillo Parado, Chihuahua on November 10, 1910.
Ciudad Juarez is the only city in the state with over one million people and is ranked eighth most populous in Mexico; Chihuahua City is ranked 16th.
Chihuahua City has one of the highest literacy rates in the country at 98%, and 76.5% of the state's population lives in cities.

entities.name: Santiago de Baca Ortiz
entities.role: Governor who quickly dissolved the new legislature and replaced it with a more pronounced Yorkino type; deputy to the first national congress and leader of the liberal party

entities.name: Gaspar de Ochoa
entities.role: Aligned with Anastasio Bustamante and organized the opposition group that arrested Governor F. Elorriaga in February 1830

entities.name: Anastasio Bustamante
entities.role: Figure Gaspar de Ochoa aligned with after Guerrero's liberal administration was overthrown in December

entities.name: F. Elorriaga
entities.role: New governor arrested by the opposition group in February 1830

entities.name: Jose Mariano Paredes
entities.role: President who issued a manifesto on May 23, 1846

entities.name: Colonel Vidal
entities.role: Led 12,000 Chihuahua men to the border to stop the American advance

entities.name: General Doniphan
entities.role: American commander who maintained camp in El Paso del Norte and marched to the state capital in February 1847

entities.name: General Price
entities.role: American general who advanced toward the state capital and began negotiations with Angel Trias on March 16, 1848

entities.name: Angel Trias
entities.role: Mexican leader in Chihuahua who sent a message asking for secession and issued an ultimatum to General Price

entities.name: Nicholas Trist
entities.role: American diplomat who signed the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo

entities.name: Luis G. Cuevas, Bernardo Couto, and Miguel Atristain
entities.role: Mexican plenipotentiary representatives who signed the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo

entities.name: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla
entities.role: Hailed as the Father of the Nation; his Grito is commemorated on September 16

entities.name: Agustin de Iturbide
entities.role: Achieved Mexican Independence in 1821, though Hidalgo is more celebrated; September 27 was the day he rode into Mexico City

entities.name: Toribio Ortega
entities.role: Madero supporter who took up arms at Cuchillo Parado, Chihuahua on November 10, 1910

entities.name: Porfirio Diaz
entities.role: President who ran again in 1910 against Francisco I. Madero and incarcerated him on election day

entities.name: Francisco I. Madero
entities.role: Opposition candidate in the 1910 presidential election against Diaz

entities.name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
entities.role: Signed February 2, 1848 to end the Mexican-American War

entities.name: Battle of El Bracito
entities.role: First battle Chihuahua fought in the war, on December 25, 1846, ending badly for Mexican forces

entities.name: Battle of Sacramento
entities.role: Most important battle in Chihuahua because it was the sole defense of the state capital

entities.name: Battle of Santa Cruz de los Rosales
entities.role: Last battle of the Mexican-American War, fought March 16, 1848 after the peace treaty was signed

entities.name: Mexican Revolution
entities.role: Began in 1910 after Diaz was announced the winner of the election by a landslide

entities.name: Chihuahua (state)
entities.role: Subject of the note; Mexican state with its capital Chihuahua City

entities.name: Ciudad Juarez
entities.role: Only city in the state with a population exceeding one million, and one of the fastest growing cities in the world

entities.name: Chihuahua City
entities.role: State capital, ranked 16th most populous in Mexico, with a 98% literacy rate

entities.name: El Paso del Norte
entities.role: Location where American forces occupied and camped awaiting supplies

entities.name: Cuchillo Parado
entities.role: Chihuahua location where Toribio Ortega took up arms on November 10, 1910

entities.name: Sand Dunes of Samalayuca
entities.role: Area in the eastern part of the state so dry that no vegetation is found

entities.name: Chihuahuan Desert
entities.role: Desert that dominates the far eastern part of the state due to low precipitation and high temperatures

entities.name: San Nicolas University
entities.role: Commissioned David Alfaro Siqueiros to paint a mural in Morelia for the 200th anniversary of Hidalgo's birth
